scope: One private dispatcher replaces four duplicate truthiness-based cleanup loops. Preserve first thrown value, ordered remaining cleanup, snapshot ownership, stale revision checks and caller SDK ownership. No public types, defaults, runtime dependencies or lockfile changes.

Six new source regressions cover seven falsy values with Object.is and independent threw flags. Existing source suite: 167 passed. Installed main/legacy/module plus source and historical controlled contracts: 470 passed, not 470 independent new regression cases.

Controlled SDK browser cases use actual old/new core controls, native MP4 and beforeUnmount callbacks; they are not adaptive SDK playback acceptance. A throwing user callback can prevent its own core control removal; sibling menus still release and the original value propagates.

Separate actual SDK browser runs use hash-pinned dash.js 4.5.2/5.2.1, local MPD media, old/new core, source topology cleanup and asynchronous formatter recovery. Windows WebKit lacks MSE; skipped actual SDK cases do not count as playback success.

Yarn packs current core and DASH, installs outside workspace, performs frozen offline reinstall, checks every file and retains checked installed copies before removing the temporary consumer. Five type modes have zero positive diagnostics and eight expected negative diagnostics each.

The three dist files, docs/compiled copies, installed copies and package architecture document have matching hashes. Scoped completion does not close full package SDK/device/release gates or authorize publishing.

Repeated input attachments are deduplicated by their original attachment SHA256. SDK event arrays retain their count and last twenty entries; buffer snapshots retain their count and last three entries; track/level state retains identifying fields. Full unabridged reports are retained at the referenced local paths with file hashes.
